plan.estimand: Minimum development sample size for survival prediction model satisfying Riley criteria: prediction accuracy (optimism-adjusted R-squared difference ≤0.05 on Nagelkerke scale) and outcome-risk absolute margin of error ≤0.05 at 95% confidence
plan.hypothesis: Prediction model with 30 candidate predictors, adjusted Cox-Snell R-squared 0.051, shrinkage 0.90 will achieve satisfactory discrimination and calibration under Riley criteria when developed in a sample of sufficient size

parameters.name: Target absolute margin of error for outcome risk

assumptions: Riley criteria applied: sample size driven by the more stringent of (1) prediction accuracy (optimism in R-squared) or (2) outcome-risk precision
Adjusted Cox-Snell R-squared 0.051 represents apparent model performance after predictor selection and fitting
Shrinkage factor 0.90 applied as specified; pmsampsize will compute optimism correction based on internal validation assumptions
Overall event rate 0.065 per person-year and mean follow-up 2.07 years represent the population under study
Prediction horizon fixed at 2 years; cumulative event rate at horizon calculated from annual rate
Nagelkerke R-squared scale used for precision requirement (applicable to survival/time-to-event models)
95% confidence level (two-sided, α=0.05) for margin of error calculation
pmsampsize 1.1.3 default internal validation approach (likely bootstrap or cross-validation) for optimism estimation
No competing risks or differential follow-up beyond mean follow-up specification
missing_information: pmsampsize package version 1.1.3 availability and exact default validation method (bootstrap or cross-validation specifics, number of replications)
Interpretation of 'adjusted Cox-Snell R-squared 0.051': is this the apparent R-squared from fitted model, or already optimism-adjusted? (Affects shrinkage application)
Justification or reference for shrinkage factor 0.90 (is this empirically derived, or a sensitivity value?)
Whether margin of error 0.05 applies to predicted risk at 2-year horizon (survival probability or cumulative incidence) or to calibration slope
pmsampsize handling of time-to-event data parameterization (Weibull vs exponential hazard, or non-parametric rate assumption)
clarification_questions: Is the adjusted Cox-Snell R-squared 0.051 the apparent performance metric from the fitted model, or is it already shrinkage-adjusted? (This determines whether pmsampsize applies additional shrinkage correction.)

The margin of error 0.05 for 'average outcome-risk'—does this refer to the absolute width of the 95% confidence interval around predicted survival/event probability at the 2-year horizon, or to calibration-in-the-large?
Should pmsampsize's internal default validation approach (e.g., bootstrap with default replications) be used, or is there a specific validation scheme you wish to specify?
Is the shrinkage factor 0.90 a conservative assumption for sensitivity analysis, or a derived optimism correction you have pre-computed?
scientific_notes: Riley et al. sample-size planning for prediction model development recommishes two simultaneous constraints: (1) optimism in model performance (apparent vs. adjusted R-squared), and (2) precision of estimated outcome risk. The required sample size is the maximum of these two.

For survival models, pmsampsize uses Cox-Snell or Nagelkerke R-squared depending on context. Cox-Snell R² ranges 0–1 but does not attain 1; Nagelkerke rescales to 0–1 for comparability with other effect sizes.
The shrinkage factor (0.90) represents expected optimism correction. Combined with predictor count (30) and apparent R² (0.051), this yields the adjusted R² used in sample-size calculation.
Event rate 0.065/person-year over mean follow-up 2.07 years implies approximately 1 - exp(-0.065 × 2.07) ≈ 0.127 cumulative event rate. Over 2-year prediction horizon: ~0.126.
Margin of error 0.05 for predicted risk at 95% confidence suggests z₀.₀₂₅ ≈ 1.96, leading to required effective sample size or number of events inversely proportional to variance of risk estimator.
